claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has improved high-temperature plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten.
The improved plastic strain and toughness of WTaTiVZr are primarily caused by mobile edge-dislocation-mediated deformation.
Pure tungsten deformation is dominated by screw dislocations.
The target alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has a single-phase BCC microstructure.
WTaTiVZr is composed of low-activation refractory elements.
WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten should be tested under identical high-temperature, strain-rate, and environmental conditions.
In-situ neutron diffraction and TEM can be used to characterize dislocations during or after loading.
Mobile edge dislocations are the relevant structural mediator in WTaTiVZr.
Edge-dislocation slip is less hindered by lattice friction than screw-dislocation slip.
Dominant edge-dislocation slip accommodates high-temperature plastic deformation more effectively than the screw-dislocation mechanism in pure tungsten.
Under high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Under high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
Under high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will show extensive edge-dislocation motion.
Pure tungsten has lower high-temperature ductility and toughness than WTaTiVZr.

The proposed behavior is limited to temperatures relevant to plasma-facing components and to microstructures that remain single-phase BCC without substantial oxidation, grain growth, or phase separation.
Prior work attributes high-temperature strength and strength retention in NbTaTiV and CrMoNbV refractory HEAs to edge dislocations.
The quantitative effects of the constituent elements on activation barriers and dislocation mobility in equimolar WTaTiVZr remain undefined.
Environmental or microstructural instabilities such as phase decomposition could alter the service behavior.
Failure to observe both a higher mobile-edge-dislocation proportion and greater plastic strain and toughness in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten would falsify the hypothesis.
